attempts.label: DANDI:000473
attempts.paper_title: Esr1+ hypothalamic-habenula neurons shape aversive states
attempts.entry_title: Aversive signals in the mPFC of Esr1-cre, Vglut2-cre, Npy-cre and control mice (Calvigioni et al. 2023)
attempts.summary: The paper's main prefrontal recording findings largely hold in this data: light activation of the LHA-LHb pathway in Vglut2-cre and Esr1-cre mice modulates more mPFC units than in controls, shifts population activity during the stimulation block, and lets prelimbic activity decode that block better. Two parts did not hold: Npy-cre mice also showed slightly more light-modulated units than controls, depending on the random seed, and the higher Esr1 tuning score was not significant, as only 7 of the paper's 10 Esr1 mice have units in the recorded areas. The persistent pupil increase could not be tested, as pupil tracking is missing. The patch-clamp, Patch-seq, anatomy and behavior findings, most of the paper, are not in this dataset.
attempts.description: Tests the Neuropixels findings of Calvigioni, Fuzik, Le Merre et al. (2023) on dandiset 000473, which holds mPFC recordings from 25 head-fixed mice during tone, optogenetic and air-puff blocks. It checks the unit selection, the GLM tuning to the light, sound and air puff, waveform classes, conditioned and comodulated units, population trajectories, clustering, activity modes and decoding of block identity. The ex vivo, anatomy and behavior experiments are not in the dandiset.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Calvigioni et al. (2023) from dandiset 000473

outcomes.statement: The dandiset's 25 sessions are the 25 NWB files of the paper's session table, and the units selected from them by the paper's rules are the units listed in the code's per-session GLM outputs.
outcomes.source: Code availability; Esr1_NPX_code at commit 85187f3, utilities/Aversion_session_description.tsv and analysis/GLM_fitted/*_tmu.mat
outcomes.quote: The code generated during this study to analyze the Neuropixels dataset is available at https://github.com/PierreLeMerre/Esr1_NPX_code
outcomes.notes: All 25 sessions match the code's session table by subject and date; the files give Vglut2-cre for 216300 and 216301, which the table lists as C57BL-6J. Over blocks 1 to 4 without saturation removal, 18 of 25 sessions give the code's tmu units index for index (4 of these have no units), below the 22 the criterion asks; 1,937 units are common, 61 are fitted here only (58 on ILA6a or ORBm6a channels, 38 in session 128516) and none are in the code's outputs only. Per genotype 492/482 (Ctl), 743/738 (Vglut2), 445/406 (Npy), 318/311 (Esr1), all within 10%. Over the whole session 4 sessions match and the counts are not within 10%. With the spikes within 1 s of the files' 'spike saturation' periods removed (the code's series), 16 sessions match. The own mean rate is a median 1.03 to 1.09 times the code's Mean_FR rate per session; the selection differs by 5 units (4,159 against 4,154). The dandiset's tuning scores correlate with the code's (Spearman r 0.95 to 0.99) and the tuned flags agree for 90 to 92% of units.
deviations: The GLM period is not stated in the Methods. Fig4g_GLM_tuning.m sets GLM_restrict = 0 (whole session) but reads binned counts from files not in the repository; the same script holds a commented restriction to blocks 1 to 4 (stop 2 s before the first block-5 trial). The code's fitted units match that restriction (no tmu unit missed, 18 of 25 sessions identical) and not the whole session (4 identical, 57 tmu units missed). The period from the session start to 2 s before block 5 is adopted as an assumption, and the whole session is shown as a variant.

Spikes within 1 s of the files' 'spike saturation' periods are removed, an assumption. The Methods say 'LFP saturation periods'; the code (RemoveSaturationSpikes, +- 1 s) reads the 'spike saturation' series, and the 'LFP saturation' series would remove 19.5 min of session 147463 including all of block 3. The code's series is used; the LFP series is run as a variant through the GLM claims (fig4g-glm-units, fig4e, fig4g-opto-tuning-score, fig4g-tuned-unit-counts), where it gives the same outcomes; it is not run for the other claims.

outcomes.statement: Optogenetic activation strongly modulates mPFC units in Vglut2-cre and Esr1-cre mice but not in Npy-cre mice, while the auditory stimuli and air puffs modulate mPFC units in all four groups.
outcomes.source: Results, Pathway-specific aversive signals in the PFC, paragraph 2; Figure 4e and Extended Data Figure 7a
outcomes.quote: We found strong modulation of mPFC units in response to optogenetic activation only in Vglut2-cre and Esr1-cre and not in Npy-cre mice, while air puffs and auditory stimuli modulated mPFC activity in all four mouse groups
outcomes.notes: Opto-tuned fraction of GLM-fitted units, Ctl 49/492 (10.0%), Vglut2 369/743 (49.7%, Fisher p = 6.9e-52), Esr1 110/317 (34.7%, p = 1.2e-17), Npy 64/443 (14.4%, p = 0.044). All four genotypes exceed chance for sound 1 (41 to 64% tuned) and air puff (37 to 50%), binomial p below 1e-290 against 0.11% and below 1e-246 against 0.25%, above the false-positive rate measured for the tuned flags on null copies of the units (18 of 7,980 tests, 0.23%, 95% CI 0.13 to 0.36%; the excess over 0.11% comes from the extreme percentiles of 1,000 shifts, which the paper's code uses too). These parts hold over the ten seeds, the whole session and the 'LFP saturation' series. Vglut2 and Esr1 are above Ctl at p of 1.1e-14 or less in each, and the lowest sound 1 and air-puff fractions of any genotype are 28.8% and 32.3% (whole session), with the largest binomial p against 0.25% at 1.3e-185. The part 'Npy does not' fails on the criterion's test with seed 0 (p = 0.044), so the claim holds in part. That failure is fragile. Over ten seeds of the shifts Npy is above Ctl at p < 0.05 in 5 (p 0.014 to 0.357); with Bonferroni for three comparisons p = 0.132; over mice the Npy fractions (0.009 to 0.277, 4 mice) do not differ from Ctl (0.037 to 0.211, 5 mice, Mann-Whitney p = 0.905), while Vglut2 (p = 0.008) and Esr1 (p = 0.030) do. Two of four Npy mice carry the excess (33/201 and 26/94). With the 'LFP saturation' series Npy is 15.5% against 10.4% (p = 0.022); over the whole session Npy is below Ctl (6.7% against 21.4%); with the code's own tuned flags Npy (14.5%) does not differ from Ctl (11.0%, p = 0.128). Second reading, block-2 PSTH over 0.7 to 1.2 s, mean z Vglut2 1.81 and Esr1 1.75 (medians 0.38 and 0.42), Ctl -0.010 and Npy 0.0004 (medians -0.14 and -0.15, p = 3.7e-11 and 2.0e-6 against 0), so in that reading p alone does not separate the genotypes. The outcome was not_reproduced before round 1 of verification and is now partially_reproduced (see verifications).

outcomes.statement: The latency of the mPFC population response to the auditory stimulus and to the air puff is similar across the four groups of mice.
outcomes.source: Results, Pathway-specific aversive signals in the PFC, paragraph 2; Extended Data Figure 7b-d
outcomes.quote: The latency of the mPFC responses to auditory stimulus and air puff was similar across the different mice
outcomes.notes: With the window before each event as baseline (1 s before the tone, 0.5 s before the air puff), tone latencies are 20 to 50 ms and lie within 20 ms across genotypes in 4 of 4 subregions under both thresholds; air-puff latencies are 60 to 90 ms and lie within 20 ms in 3 of 4 (PL spreads 30 ms). With the 1 s before the trial start as baseline, the air puff agrees in 2 of 4 subregions under both thresholds, because the Vglut2 rate in ORBm and PL is still above the pre-trial baseline at puff onset (0.7 s after the blue noise).
deviations: The criterion says 'pre-event baseline' without its length; 1 s before the tone (the Methods' pre-tone baseline) and 0.5 s before the air puff (between the end of the blue noise and the puff) are assumed, as the literal reading of the criterion; the pre-trial baseline, which fails for the air puff, is shown.

outcomes.quote: This unbiased classification identified two distinct clusters containing opto-modulated units (‘opto’ clusters), showing time-locked or sustained opto-modulation, and these units belonged to Vglut2-cre and Esr1-cre mice
outcomes.notes: Clusters 1 and 2 (64 and 87 units) have opto as most common primary tuning (62% and 70%) and all their units come from Vglut2 (61, 74) and Esr1 (3, 13) mice. The quality control keeps all 1,995 fitted units, outside the tolerance of 1,770 or 1,788 (+- 10%), so the expected count is not met. Under the code's rule (more than 200 bins above 0.5 Hz in the smoothed trial averages) the fewest active bins of any fitted unit is 454, and units fitted at 2 Hz or more cannot fail it. Unsmoothed averages keep 1,995, z-scored rates (|z| > 0.5) 1,974 and single trials 266; keeping 1,770 would need a cutoff of 1,308 active bins. The 5-point gausswin of the code is the same kernel as the Methods' Gaussian of sigma 0.8 bins and gives the same clusters, so it is a check, not a separate reading.

outcomes.statement: Five of the clusters ('state' clusters) contain units whose baseline firing rate rises in one block or ramps across blocks.
outcomes.source: Results, Pathway-specific aversive signals in the PFC, paragraph 5; Extended Data Figure 9b-g and Supplementary Table 9
outcomes.quote: Interestingly, we observed five clusters (‘state’ clusters) with units showing a significant increase in baseline firing rate in one block or ramping baseline activity across blocks
outcomes.notes: 13 of 15 clusters have a significant block pair (Wilcoxon, Bonferroni 6) with monotonic or one-block-rise baseline means; with the code's rank-sum test, 9. Both opto clusters are among them. The rule is weak: only clusters 6 and 8 fail it, so the count cannot single out five state clusters, which the paper names subjectively.
deviations: The clustered units are the units fitted with the GLM over blocks 1 to 4, an assumption (see code-outputs-link); the whole-session period is not run for this claim.
What counts as a rise in one block is read here as the block with the highest mean being significantly above at least one other block, a choice.

outcomes.statement: Projection onto the 'opto OR air puff' mode separates block 2 from block 1 only in Esr1-cre and Vglut2-cre mice, and the 'state' mode separates the four blocks completely across time.
outcomes.source: Results, Pathway-specific aversive signals in the PFC, paragraph 7; Figure 4i
outcomes.quote: we found that the modulation along the activity mode capturing the optogenetic effect (‘opto OR air puff’) was specific to the activation of Esr1+ or Vglut2+ LHA–LHb neurons in block 2 ... the ‘state’ mode (baseline activity in block 4 versus block 1) captured distinct population activity modes in each of the four blocks, with complete separation of the block projections across time
outcomes.notes: Under all three unit readings and both window sets, (i) the block 2 minus block 1 difference on the 'opto OR air puff' mode over 0.7 to 1.2 s is larger in Vglut2 and Esr1 than in Ctl and Npy (Methods windows, reading (a), Vglut2 199.4, Esr1 26.4, Ctl 1.9, Npy 1.6), and (ii) the ranges of the four blocks on the 'state' mode do not overlap (0 of 6 pairs).

findings.statement: Sessions 216300 and 216301 are labelled Vglut2-cre in the files' subject genotype, while the paper's code lists them as C57BL-6J controls. With the files' labels the dandiset has 3 controls and 7 Vglut2-cre mice, where the paper has 5 and 5.
The files give sex F for 10 of the 25 mice; the Fig. 4 legend states that all data were acquired in male mice.

Four sessions (128515, 258412, 259112, 273853) have no unit whose main channel is labelled ACAd, PL, ILA or ORBm (their probes are labelled in ORBl, ORBvl, AON, MOs and other areas), so only 21 of the 25 mice contribute units to the paper's analyses, 7 of the 10 Esr1-cre mice and 4 of the 5 Npy-cre mice. The paper reports 25 mice and n = 10 Esr1-cre mice for its tests.
The trials table's opto_power column is 0 in every trial, and the OptogeneticSeries (unit 'mW') peaks at 0.9 to 3.3 per session, where the paper states 6 mW in block 2.

The trials table holds blocks 9 to 12 (light at 5, 10 and 20 Hz and a block without frequency) and, in two sessions, a block 0, none described in the paper or the files; 259112 has 100 trials in block 1 and some blocks have 51 to 61 trials where the paper states 50.
The trials table's opto_pulse_ts column has no unit or description; its values are the light-pulse times multiplied by about 11,574.
Sessions 268951, 273853 and 273858 hold 629, 520 and 570 tone events in AudStim_10kHz, where the trials table has 200 tone trials; the extra events have no trials.
The airpuff_duration column gives 20 ms, where the paper states a 50 ms air puff.

The optogenetic stimulus site is 'LHA' in all 25 files, while the paper stimulates LHA somata in retrograde and LHb terminals in anterograde Esr1-cre mice; the files do not say which Esr1-cre mice are which (the code's table does).

The files hold two saturation series. The 'LFP saturation' series of session 147463 spans 1500 to 2671 s, all of block 3; removing spikes in it, as the Methods' words say, silences block 3 for all 209 units of that session. The paper's code uses the 'spike saturation' series (274 s at most).

Fig4g_GLM_tuning.m sets GLM_restrict = 0 (fit over the whole session), but the code's fitted units (tmu) match a fit over blocks 1 to 4 only (all 1,937 found, 18 of 25 sessions identical); over the whole session 57 of them are not fitted. The binned counts it reads are not in the repository.
The code's GLM outputs omit 61 units that pass its own selection on the dandiset, 58 of them on ILA6a or ORBm6a channels (38 in session 128516).

Question for the paper's authors: over which period was the GLM fitted (the whole session or blocks 1 to 4), and which saturation series was used to remove spikes? The tuned-unit counts and the Npy result of Fig. 4e depend on it: over blocks 1 to 4 Npy has 14.4% opto-tuned units against 10.0% in controls (p = 0.044), over the whole session 6.7% against 21.4%.

Question for the paper's authors: how was the onset latency of Extended Data Fig. 7b-d detected, and against which baseline? With the window before the air puff the genotypes agree within 20 ms in 3 of 4 subregions; with the pre-trial baseline only in 2.
The Patch-seq deposit (BioStudies S-BSST1069) labels cells with Ephys_Category codes 1 to 6 and gives no mapping of the codes to the paper's six neuron types.

The pupil and eye tracking of Fig. 4f and Extended Data Fig. 7g-j are not in the dandiset; one file (128514) holds an eye-area trace. The LHA optotagging recordings of Extended Data Fig. 1e-j are not in it either.

Supplementary Table 6 reports N = 10 Esr1-cre and N = 5 Npy-cre mice for the tuning-score test (Esr1 corrected p = 0.045), but the code's own GLM outputs, like the dandiset, have units for only 7 Esr1-cre and 4 Npy-cre mice. The table also prints Bonferroni-corrected p values above 1.

Question for the paper's authors: how did the clustering quality control (Methods, Hierarchical clustering) reduce 1,945 units to 1,788 (Methods) or 1,770 (Results)? The code's rule, more than 200 of 1,600 bins above 0.5 Hz in the smoothed trial averages, cannot drop a unit fitted with the GLM, whose mean rate is at least 2 Hz; on the dandiset the fewest active bins of any fitted unit is 454.

The units table has no curation label column, so the Methods' selection of 'good' units cannot be checked on the files. In session 128514 the series named eye_area is described as a smoothed pupil trace, so it is not clear whether it measures the eye or the pupil.

disagreements.reason: Vglut2 and Esr1 opto fractions exceed Ctl and sound 1 and air puff exceed chance in all four genotypes, but the Npy opto fraction is also higher than Ctl at p = 0.044, which breaks 'Npy does not'. A two-sided unit- level Fisher test pools units across mice (one Npy mouse contributes 33 of 201 units); without a per-mouse view or a correction for three comparisons the result is fragile, and tuned flags from one seed could change it. The real false-positive rate is about 0.1% for the negative tail plus 0.05 to 0.1% for the positive tail, which does not matter at about 40%. In the second reading Ctl and Npy also give significant Wilcoxon p with negative medians.

entries.title: Aversive signals in the mPFC of Esr1-cre, Vglut2-cre, Npy-cre and control mice (Calvigioni et al. 2023)
entries.description: Tests the Neuropixels findings of Calvigioni, Fuzik, Le Merre et al. (2023) on dandiset 000473, which holds mPFC recordings from 25 head-fixed mice during tone, optogenetic and air-puff blocks. It checks the unit selection, the GLM tuning to the light, sound and air puff, waveform classes, conditioned and comodulated units, population trajectories, clustering, activity modes and decoding of block identity. The ex vivo, anatomy and behavior experiments are not in the dandiset.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Calvigioni et al. (2023) from dandiset 000473
